title: A Phone Call About the Uncle Nobody Wants to Host
script: Ratna: [thoughtful] Ilham, tell me honestly, is it my turn to host Uncle Zul this year, or have I simply lost track of the rotation entirely.
Ilham: Technically it's mine, but I'll confess I've been quietly hoping you'd forget the rotation existed at all.
Ratna: [carefully] I have not forgotten. I have simply been pretending very convincingly, apparently unsuccessfully, given this call.
Ilham: He's exhausting, Ratna, I won't pretend otherwise. An entire weekend of unsolicited commentary on my career choices, my weight, my continued bachelorhood.
Ratna: [reflective] And yet he flew here alone after Auntie passed, with nobody left to tell him his commentary lands rather badly these days.
Ilham: I hadn't thought about it from that particular angle, honestly. I'd mostly been thinking about my own weekend, selfishly.
Ratna: [honestly] Adab doesn't require us to enjoy hosting him. It just requires us to host him properly regardless of enjoyment, which are entirely separate obligations.
Ilham: That's an uncomfortably precise distinction to hear at eight in the morning, over the phone, no less.
Ratna: [gently] Precise distinctions are usually the ones worth hearing early, before the day gives us a convenient excuse to forget them.
Ilham: Fine. I'll host him properly, and I'll try genuinely listening rather than merely enduring his commentary this particular time.
Ratna: [calmly] That's more than the rotation technically required of you. Thank you for actually hearing me out on this.
Ilham: Will you come for dinner one evening, at least, so I'm not entirely alone absorbing the commentary myself.
Ratna: [encouraging] I'll come for one evening, strategically positioned between his opinions on my career and his opinions on yours.
Ilham: Fair distribution. We'll call it shared adab, since apparently neither of us can sustain it solo for an entire weekend.
Ratna: [seriously] Nobody expects solo sustainability, Ilham. That's rather the entire point of family showing up in shifts, isn't it.

quiz.question: What is Ratna calling Ilham to clarify?
options: Whose turn it is to host Uncle Zul this year
Who will pay for a family trip
Who will plan a birthday party
Whether to sell a family property
quiz.explanation: Ratna calls to clarify whether it's her turn to host Uncle Zul or if she's lost track of the rotation.

quiz.question: What does Ilham admit he was hoping regarding Ratna?
options: That she would host every year permanently
That she would forget the hosting rotation existed
That she would refuse to speak to Uncle Zul
That she would move away entirely
quiz.explanation: Ilham confesses he was quietly hoping Ratna would forget the rotation existed at all.

quiz.question: What does Ratna point out about Uncle Zul's situation since Auntie passed?
options: He has remarried recently
He no longer wants to visit
He flew here alone, with nobody left to tell him his commentary lands badly
He has stopped speaking to the family
quiz.explanation: Ratna notes he flew in alone after Auntie passed, with no one left to tell him his commentary lands badly.

quiz.question: How does Ratna distinguish adab from enjoyment in this context?
options: She says adab requires genuinely enjoying every guest
She says adab is irrelevant to family hosting
She says enjoyment is the only real measure of adab
She says adab doesn't require enjoying hosting him, just hosting him properly regardless
quiz.explanation: Ratna explains adab doesn't require enjoying hosting him, only hosting him properly, which are separate obligations.

quiz.question: What do Ratna and Ilham agree to do by the end of the call?
options: Ilham will host properly and Ratna will join for one dinner to share the load
Ratna will host alone instead
They will ask another relative to host instead
They will cancel the visit entirely
quiz.explanation: Ilham agrees to host properly and Ratna agrees to come for one dinner so he isn't entirely alone with it.

quiz.question: What principle reframes the family's hosting obligation?
options: A difficult relative should be hosted only when pleasant
They need not enjoy Uncle Zul, but should host him properly
The family should ignore his grief to protect their weekend
Hosting becomes optional once the rotation is inconvenient
quiz.explanation: Ratna distinguishes enjoyment from the obligation to offer a difficult relative proper care.

quiz.question: Which detail most supports Ratna's call for compassion?
options: Uncle Zul has always preferred to spend holidays alone
Ilham has never met Uncle Zul's family
Uncle Zul has been alone since Auntie passed away
The family cancelled the annual hosting rotation
quiz.explanation: Ratna asks Ilham to see his uncle's difficult behaviour alongside the loneliness that followed Auntie's death.

quiz.question: How do the cousins qualify the demand placed on one host?
options: One relative should absorb all discomfort to prove sincerity
Hosting is only valid if it happens without any support
A demanding guest should be confronted by the whole family at once
Family members can share the care rather than leave one host alone
quiz.explanation: Ratna offers to join dinner, showing that care can be shared without withdrawing proper hospitality.

quiz.question: Which stance does Ratna take toward Uncle Zul's difficult behaviour?
options: She asks for compassion without denying that he can be exhausting
She treats his comments as harmless because he is elderly
She argues that relatives must enjoy every family visit
She recommends leaving him alone after a difficult comment
quiz.explanation: Ratna acknowledges the strain while inviting Ilham to consider his uncle's bereavement and isolation.

quiz.question: What implication follows from the cousins' final arrangement?
options: The rotation should be abandoned after any complaint
Family care can be shared while preserving a demanding relative's dignity
Hosting requires accepting every hurtful remark without response
Bereavement removes the need for ordinary family boundaries
quiz.explanation: They share the practical burden while still committing to host Uncle Zul with care.
